# Thursday: set up your learning with ChatGPT {.unnumbered}

[Week 1 hands-on session · Thursday, October 15, 10 a.m. · 60 minutes]{.subtitle .lead}

Today you open ChatGPT Edu and use it for something useful: you write your
own learning goals for the course, and the journal you will keep each week.
You leave with two things you made and will use again.

You do not need any experience with chatbots. If this is your first time,
that is fine. ChatGPT will ask the questions; you answer them.

## What you need

- A laptop with a web browser.
- Your **ChatGPT Edu** account. Sign in at [chatgpt.com](https://chatgpt.com)
  with your university email. If you have not set it up yet, follow the
  Canvas page "Get your ChatGPT Edu account" before class.
- Nothing about patients. Today is about you and your learning.

## The plan

| Time | Step |
|---|---|
| 10 min | 1. Sign in and get set up |
| 20 min | 2. Write your learning goals with ChatGPT |
| 15 min | 3. Design your learning journal |
| 10 min | 4. Save your work, and share one goal |
| 5 min | 5. What happens next week |

## Sign in and get set up

1. Go to [chatgpt.com](https://chatgpt.com) and sign in with your university
   email.
2. Check the bottom left of the screen. It should say
   **"CU - Anschutz (Edu)"**. If it does not, say so now and we will sort it
   out together.
3. Make a **project** for this course. Look for **Projects** in the left
   sidebar, make a new one, and name it "AI in Medicine". A project keeps
   your chats for this course together, so you can come back to them.
4. Start a new chat inside the project.

## Write your learning goals

Copy this prompt into the chat. Fill in the part in brackets first.

```
I'm a fourth-year medical student starting a 4-week
course on AI in medicine. I'm applying in
[your specialty, or "undecided"].

Interview me, one question at a time, about what I
want from this course: what I have tried with AI so
far, what worries me about it, and where AI might
help my work as a resident.

After about six questions, suggest 3 to 5 learning
goals, written in my own words, each with one small
thing I could try this week. Then ask me what I want
to change.
```

Answer each question in a sentence or two. There are no wrong answers. If
you are not sure what you want yet, say that; it is a useful answer.

When ChatGPT suggests your goals, read them and **make them yours**. Change
anything that does not sound like you. Ask for a goal to be smaller, bigger,
or more specific to your specialty. Keep going until you would be happy to
show them to a colleague.

## Design your learning journal

Each week you write a short [learning journal](learning-journal.qmd) entry.
Now you design your own version of it. In the same chat, copy this prompt:

```
Using the goals we just wrote, help me design a
weekly learning journal I can fill in within 30
minutes. Make it a short markdown template.

It must include these five course questions:
1. What I chose to learn, and why
2. How AI helped, and where it got in the way
   (including one time I felt I needed to check
   the AI: how I checked, and what I found)
3. What surprised me
4. What changed for me
5. What I used, and whether it was worth my time

Add one or two headings of your own that connect
each entry to my goals. Then fill in a sample entry
for this week so I can see how it works.
```

Read the template. Move, rename, or cut the extra headings until it suits
how you think. The five course questions stay.

## Save your work, and share one goal

- Copy your final goals and your journal template into a document you keep:
  a notes app, Word, or Google Docs. Name it "AI in Medicine journal".
- Your chat stays in the "AI in Medicine" project, so you can return to it.

Then, if you are willing, read one of your goals aloud or type it in the
chat. Hearing what classmates want from the course is often the most useful
part of the hour.

## What happens next week

Your journal template is where your week 1 entry goes, due Thursday night in
Canvas. Each week after that:

1. Open your "AI in Medicine" project and start a new chat for the week.
2. Paste in your journal document and tell ChatGPT what you tried.
3. Ask it to help you write this week's entry in your template.
4. Read it, make it yours, and submit it.

A new chat each week works better than one long chat. Very long chats lose
track of what was said in the middle; you will see why in Wednesday's
session. Your document carries what matters from week to week.

## Three rules, every session

1. **No patient information** in a chatbot unless your hospital has approved
   that tool for it.
2. **Make it yours.** Read what it gives you and change what does not fit.
3. **You sign what you submit.** Whatever helped you write it, it is yours.
